title: Couple Who Birthed Another Family's Baby in Horrifying IVF Mix-Up Will Keep Her Permanently | TRUTH Press
text:
A Florida couple at the center of a horrifying IVF mix-up have vowed to remain their baby girl’s “permanent” parents.
They reached a custody agreement with the child’s biological parents after she was born from the wrong embryo.
A Permanent Family Tiffany Score and Steven Mills confirmed the identities of their 6-month-old daughter Shea’s genetic parents.
They have “come to a mutually devised custody agreement” with them, according to court papers filed Friday.
Under the deal, the couple will “continue as the permanent custodial parents of their daughter.”
The details of the arrangement are being kept private.
“I’m glad the parties have reached an agreement while this child is relatively young,” Orlando Judge Margaret Schreiber said Monday.
The judge welcomed the resolution during a court hearing.
How The Mix-Up Unfolded Score and Mills sued the Fertility Center of Orlando in January.
They also named its head reproductive endocrinologist, Dr. Milton McNichol.
The suit alleged the clinic implanted the wrong embryo in April 2025.
The hopeful mother only discovered the error after giving birth to a “non-Caucasian” Shea on Dec. 11, 2025.
DNA testing confirmed Shea was not genetically related to them and was 100% South Asian.
The couple loved her nonetheless.
Building a Bond The couple’s lawyer, Jack Scarola, said his clients are committed to respecting the genetic parents’ privacy.
“They have begun and intend to continue to foster a relationship of friendship and trust” with the other couple, he said.
The parents have spoken movingly about their devotion to Shea.
“Only one thing is as absolutely certain today as it was on the day our daughter was born,” they previously said.
“We will love and will be this child’s parents forever,” they added.
The Legal Road Ahead Score and Mills told the judge they chose a new medical center for any future IVF.
Their remaining embryo has been moved there.
That embryo will be tested for parentage before they “determine next steps.”
They said information from the Fertility Center of Orlando “revealed laboratory-clinic errors.”
They believe that could help speed their case along.
Clinic Set to Close The couple had three embryos frozen with the Longwood-based clinic in 2020.
The first was implanted and ended with Score miscarrying.
The clinic had another embryo, and it was unclear what happened to the third.
The Fertility Center of Orlando said it would shutter by May 20 after “thoughtful consideration.”
